public_rationale: Research documents the harmful-content mechanism Zitron describes. It does not establish the further claim that this mechanism was causing sustained platform decline. Facebook's reported worldwide monthly audience also grew in 2023, although that does not disprove deterioration in particular markets or in experience quality. The causal assertion remains unsettled.
limitations: The meaning of platform decline materially affects the assessment.
The selected-page study is not a representative measurement of Facebook's entire content supply.
Company audience disclosures do not establish why people stayed or left.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that prioritizing engagement over experience quality is causing sustained deterioration in Facebook's audience or retention.
The surrounding post discusses audience trends from May 2021 through April 2024. That is the assessment period.
Examples of harmful recommendations establish a possible mechanism, but do not by themselves establish platform decline or its cause.
This assesses the present causal assertion, not the separate forecast of Facebook's eventual death.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable Facebook audience or retention measurements show sustained deterioration during the described period, and credible causal evidence attributes a material part of it to the stated engagement incentives.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable measurements and credible causal evidence establish that the stated incentives did not produce the alleged sustained deterioration. Growth in one audience measure alone is insufficient.
